sights.w: Walnut Hill rowhouse where singer, actor and activist Paul Robeson lived with his sister from 1966 until his death in 1976 — NRHP-listed (2000), now a museum with lectures, concerts and exhibits; the block of Walnut St is co-named for him.

Six-acre Cedar Park/Walnut Hill green (Black Oak Park, 1903–10) renamed for Malcolm X in 1995 — a hub for West Philly drumming circles, festivals and community events, a block from the restored Malcolm X mural building.

sights.address: N 3rd St between Poplar St & Girard Ave, Northern Liberties, Philadelphia, PA 19123
sights.w: Two-acre community park on a former tannery site, built and still run by the Northern Liberties Neighbors Association without city support — a Project for Public Spaces case study; hayrides, summer movies and the neighbourhood's Welcome America festival.

Horace Trumbauer's 1893 castle-mansion for sugar magnate William Welsh Harrison, Beaver College's home from 1929 and now Arcadia University's centrepiece — a National Historic Landmark (1985); student-led tours and October ghost tours. (HELD lead from W3 cleared.)

sources.name: Project for Public Spaces
sources.credible: Nonprofit planning organisation (since 1975) whose placemaking case studies document notable public spaces — corroborating.
